newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa says 10,000 new jobs from tourism boom.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa says 10,000 new jobs from tourism boom.

text.p: Tourism boomed in South Africa last year resulting in some 10,000 new jobs, tourism minister Pallo Jordan said on Friday.
"In the area of tourism, this past year has probably been South Africa's best success story in years," Jordan told a news briefing at parliament in Cape Town.
He said preliminary figures indicated tourist arrivals between January and September last year rose eight percent against the same period in 1995.
"The indications about the high season, that is September to January, are that it will be much higher than that," he said.
"There are clear indications that 1996 was a boom year for tourism. One of the indirect consequences was that in tourism, something like 10,000 new jobs were created.
"It is an area of growth which we think has great potential in terms of job creation nd creation of foreign exchange."
Jordan said signs of lower hotel occupancy were deceptive because there had been a shift to guest houses, lodges, and bed and breakfast establishments. Hotel room prices had also risen sharply.

"The biggest challenge that faces us is constructing a firm alliance between ourselves and the private sector. We have embarked on a good dialogue with the Tourism Business Council of South Africa," he said.
Jordan also said his department was "centrally involved" in the Maputo and Lebombo development corridors. "Both will entail two trans-frontier park initiatives," he said.
